title: A 48-facet plinth about 40 mm across, its facets softened, unioned onto a 4 mm plate
from: A round of the seam where softened flat facets meet a plate, rolled across the facets as a swept blend. It builds a valid, watertight solid at every size, and reads wrong. Up to 1.7 mm a handful of rail edges at the lifted vertex fail (3 to 7): the rail rides a seam between a wall facet and a steep facet and is tangent to neither, and sliver strip facets there inherit the seam's soft mark on the rail. At 2.5 mm the ball is too large for the wall, and the solve against the side surfaces rides the plinth's hard top rim, tangent nowhere: 187 rail edges read wrong. The plinth is drawn from triangles with 20 µm of noise, its middle ring buried 3 mm in the plate; one vertex of that ring sits 3.9 µm above the plate. Generated by a script: 48 sides, two bands of triangles.

cases.note: The seam as the loop of the plate's top face around the plinth. The plinth wall leans in 13 degrees and stands 1.4 mm above the plate, so a ball touches it within its height up to about 1.8 mm.
The same seam picked by a click on one of its edges, on the far side from the lifted vertex, as a user picks it.
